Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that's it from the coverage of this game and also the inaugural edition of the Women's U-19 T20 World Cup. This tournament has certainly raised the bar for Women's cricket and that is a huge boost for the game of cricket. Well then, the focus now will shift to the ICC Women's T20 World Cup will begin from February 10th. Make sure you do not miss any action. Until then, take care and goodbye!

Just after the interview, Shafali Verma collects the trophy and lines-up with her squad for a team-photo. So, India Women Under-19 are shining under the sun here in South Africa as they become the first ever U-19 Women's side to lift the World Cup. Smiles all across the Indian camp and they truly lit the tournament with the way they played.

Now, it is time for the victorious team to collect their medallions and once it is done. Shafali Verma, the captain of India Women Under-19 joins in for a chat. She informs that all the girls were incredible. It feels really good and is glad every one is backing each other in the side. Verma is unable to hold back her happy tears. She credits the backroom staff for their tremendous support. She thanks BCCI to give her this side and she is proud to win the cup with this squad. Praises Shweta Sehrawat's consistent performances with the blade. Ends by saying that she will aim to win yet another trophy in February but this time with the Indian Women's team.

England Women Under-19 players are now called out to collect their medals which is followed by another chat with Grace Scrivens. This time she focuses on the team aspect. She says that they are gutted and feel it was the batting that let them down. Adds that their batting has been so good throughout the tournament but just couldn't do well today. Reckons that they went with the fearless mindset with the bat but it did not work out today. Shares that it was a huge privilege to lead the team and the support from the senior team and family has been awesome.

Grace Scrivens, the skipper of England Women Under-19 wins the Player of the Series award for her all-round effort. She starts by saying that she is pretty pleased with her performance over the course. Mentions that it is her first time playing overseas and is taking back a lot of learnings here.

Titas Sadhu wins the Player of the Match award for her exceptional spell with the new ball. She says that it is a surreal feeling and they had been looking forward to this day for a long time. Adds that they had a plan and it was all about execution. Shares that she does not feel lonely despite being the only pacer in the side. Reckons that they had a good idea where to bowl on this wicket having played a couple of games here. Ends by thanking her coaches.
Stay tuned for the presentation...

Archana Devi is up next for a chat. She says that it is a brilliant feeling and she is happy that they completed the job they came here for. Adds that she will look to perform well whenever she gets a chance. Ends by saying the fielding practice resulted in her taking that one-handed stunner.
Gongadi Trisha also joins for a flash interview. She says that it is a proud moment since this is their first World Cup. Shares that she is super happy and they had been waiting for this day.

Nooshin Al Khadeer, the Head Coach of India, is in for a quick chat. She says that it is a fabulous feeling and they have been waiting for this moment for so long. Adds that the belief shown by the girls was everything even after losing to Australia earlier in the competition. Shares that they had goosebumps right from the time of national anthem till the time they won. Ends by saying that god has been kind and she is keeping it simple.

Earlier in the innings, after being put to bat England Women Under-19 looked down and out right from the the get go, as they started losing wickets from the very first over. No one other Ryana Macdonald-Gay turned with the blade for England. It was once again a sorry performance with the bat for England in this competition. India Women Under-19 were exceptionaly good with the ball. Titas Sadhu set the tone and soon, the spinners came into the picture and never let the English batters breathe easily. Eventually, England Women Under-19 team's winning streak was broken.

England Women Under-19 bowlers did not have much to fight for here. Nonetheless, England started quite positively and saw a glimmer of hope once they saw the back of Shafali Verma who was looking in good touch. Soon, Grace Scrivens got the better of Shweta Sehrawat. Although, they could not find the third wicket as soon as they would've wanted too and that's where the game slipped away from them. Alexa Stonehouse and Hannah L Baker took a wicket each as well but in a losing cause.

Soumya Tiwari stays out till the very end and scores the winning run here. In no time, she is robbed by her team-mates who rush over the ropes and begin the celebrations for India. And, the Indian squad is into their victory lap here. The crowd is getting in on the act as well. India were off to a sparkling start thanks to a brisk innings of Shafali Verma. Although, India Women Under-19 were put under some pressure early-on their opening pair was sent back in a jiffy. Soumya Tiwari and Gongadi Trisha though came out at a precarious situation but they held their nerves really well. The two stitched a crucial stand to get their side near the victory line.

The final chapter of the ICC Women's U-19 T20 World Cup comes to an end and it is India that wins the inaugural edition of this tournament. What a day this is for Indian cricket. England could not replicate their heroic effort from the semi-finals against Australia and failed to get over the line here.

THAT'S IT! India Women Under-19 are the champions of the inaugural ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup! Hannah L Baker bowls this one short and on off, Soumya Tiwari punches this one off the back foot towards cover. The fielder there fumbles and that is enough for India Women Under-19 to get over the line. Indian players charge onto the field with the tricolour and these are exceptional scenes.
Flighted, fuller on off, Soumya Tiwari goes for the drive but misses. The keeper takes the bails off but Soumya Tiwari was well in.
SCORES LEVEL! Floated and full, outside off. Soumya Tiwari leans in and lofts it over covers. They take two runs.
Flatter and on off, defended out.
Flighted delivery, fuller outside off, Soumya Tiwari leans forward and pushes it to cover.
Short and outside off, Soumya Tiwari dabs this one straight to backward point.
Shorter delivery on off, Hrishita Basu pushes this one off the back foot to mid-wicket.
Hrishita Basu is the new batter in.

OUT! BOWLED! Gongadi Trisha goes for the glory shot and perishes! Alexa Stonehouse bowls it on a good length on middle, a hint of inward movement, Gongadi Trisha tries to whip this one across the line and pays the price. Does not account for the swing and ends up getting her off-stump pegged back. Nothing but a consolation wicket for Alexa Stonehouse and England Women Under-19.

FOUR! Cracking shot by Gongadi Trisha! Alexa Stonehouse bowls this one on a length outside off, Gongadi Trisha uses her feet and drives this one hard through covers for a boundary. India Women Under-19 are nearly there.
Another good-length delivery at the batter, Gongadi Trisha clips this one straight to mid-wicket.
Loud shout but turned down! On a good length on leg, Gongadi Trisha gets forward to defend but misses and gets hit on the front leg.
Alexa Stonehouse bowls this one back of a length, angling away on off, Gongadi Trisha uses the pace of the delivery and steers this one past backward point for a couple of runs.
Fuller outside off, Soumya Tiwari goes for the drive away from her body but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Another fullish delivery, Soumya Tiwari fails to get underneath the delivery and toe-ends it to mid off.
Fullish delivery at the batter by Ellie Anderson, Gongadi Trisha clips this one to the left of mid-wicket and takes a single.
WIDE! Ellie Anderson sprays down the leg side, bowls it on a fuller length, Gongadi Trisha tries to get some bat on it as went for the slog but misses.
Back of a length outside off, Gongadi Trisha shapes to pull this one but fails to time this one well. Ends up pushing it back to the bowler.
FOUR! Consecutive boundaries. This time off her front foot. It is full, straying on the pads. Trisha flicks it aerially over square leg. It races away to the fence.
FOUR! Shot of authority! It is a short ball, on middle and leg. Trisha stands tall and pulls it powerfully through mid-wicket for a cracking boundary.
Pace from both ends as Ellie Anderson comes on to bowl.
Alexa Stonehouse dishes a full-length ball, in the channel, moving away. Soumya Tiwari tries to go for the drive but gets beaten on the outside edge.
A length ball, on leg. Trisha stays back and flicks it through square leg for a single. 50 is up for India.
Full and on the pads. Trisha tucks it to short mid-wicket. Alexa Stonehouse is not giving any room here.
Much fuller, around off, angling across. Trisha pushes it gently towards mid off.
Soumya Tiwari rotates the strike now. It is full and on off. Tiwari gets it down to third man off the outside edge.
A length ball, angled across, on off. Tiwari strokes it to cover.

Drinks break! India Women Under-19 now just need 21 runs off 60 balls. England Women Under-19 haven't been able to cause any problems since the departure of Shweta Sehrawat. Only a miracle can make is possible for England to get their noses in front now. They now bring Alexa Stonehouse into the attack.
Short and on off, Soumya Tiwari goes back on the back foot and turns this one towards deep square leg. Retains the strike with a single.
Another floated delivery, full on middle, Gongadi Trisha gets forward and works it down to long on for a run.
Flighted, full on off, Soumya Tiwari leans forward and knocks it down to long on for a single.
Fuller at the pads, Gongadi Trisha clips this one to deep square leg for a single.
Another full delivery, this time on middle, Gongadi Trisha drives this one down the ground but can only find mid off.
Floated, fuller on off, Gongadi Trisha drives this one hard on the off side but fails to get it past cover.
Another short delivery on off, Soumya Tiwari pushes this one off the back foot to cover.
FOUR! Short and outside off, Soumya Tiwari picks the length early and rocks back in her crease. Slaps this one just wide of the diving cover-point fielder and collects a boundary.
Another flighted delivery, fuller on off, Soumya Tiwari plays it with the turn and lofts it over cover for a couple of runs.
Tossed up, fuller on off, Soumya Tiwari pushes this one from the front foot to cover.
Flighted delivery, full at the stumps, Soumya Tiwari gets forward and defends it with a straight bat.
Josie Groves floats this one, full on off, Gongadi Trisha uses her feet and works it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Fuller and angling in on middle and leg, Soumya Tiwari blocks this one out on the leg side.

FOUR! Sophia Smale fires this one full but down the leg side, Soumya Tiwari gets inside the line of the delivery and clips this one towards fine leg. Grace Scrivens performs the chase and does put in a dive but fails to prevent the boundary.
Short and at the stumps, Gongadi Trisha stays on the back foot and punches it down to long on for a single.
Short and on middle, Gongadi Trisha punches this one towards extra cover. The fielder there fumbles and Soumya Tiwari wants to sneak in a single but gets sent back just in time by Gongadi Trisha.
Short and quicker on off, Gongadi Trisha goes back in her crease and defends this one on the off side.
Tossed up, fullish delivery on off, Gongadi Trisha pushes this one back to the bowler.
Josie Groves bowls a low full toss on off, Soumya Tiwari drives this one firmly but straight to extra cover.
Josie Groves shortens her length and bowls it short at the batter, Gongadi Trisha stays on the back foot and chips this one uppishly towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Fuller outside off, Gongadi Trisha taps this one from the back foot to cover-point for a dot.
Flighted delivery, full on middle, Gongadi Trisha gets forward and defends this one on the off side.
Short and flatter on off, Gongadi Trisha steers this one on the bounce towards first slip.
Josie Groves starts with a loosener, bowls it short on middle, Soumya Tiwari pulls this one through mid-wicket for a single.
Change. Josie Groves comes into the attack now.

Pushed through quicker, short around off, Gongadi Trisha dabs this one off the back foot to backward point. At the end of the Powerplay, India Women Under-19 have scored 30 runs for the loss of two wickets.
Slower and short on off, Soumya Tiwari goes back in her crease and works it to the left of mid-wicket for a single.
Flighted, fullish delivery on off, Soumya Tiwari looks to push this one down the ground but toe-ends it to cover.
Short and turning in on off, Soumya Tiwari goes back and blocks this one out on the off side.
Low full toss on off, Gongadi Trisha drives it to the right of the bowler for a single.
Short and turning in on off, Soumya Tiwari hangs back and pulls this one hard towards deep mid-wicket for a single.

DROPPED! A tough chance goes abegging. It is tossed up, full and outside off. Tiwari goes for a booming drive but gets a thick outside edge on it. The ball flies towards Grace Scrivens at first slip. She gets two good hands on it but it does not stick on this occasion.

FOUR! This boundary surely spoils a tidy over for Hannah L Baker. It is tossed up, on off. Soumya Tiwari chips it over covers. It races away to the fence. Soumya Tiwari holds the position after her stroke. What a way to get off the mark.
Around off, pushed to point.
Full and outside off. Tiwari pushes it out tentatively to covers.
A bit short, outside off, turning away with some extra bounce. Soumya Tiwari tries to cut it away but misses.
On middle and leg. Tiwari eases it back to the bowler.
Hannah L Baker into her third over now.
A dot ball to finish the over! Grace Scrivens starts her spell with a successful over. The tension is ramping up a touch here. It is full and on off. Trisha defends it out watchfully.
This is pushed through quicker, full and on off. Gongadi Trisha dabs it down to third man and collects a brace.
Gongadi Trisha comes out to bat.

OUT! CAUGHT! Grace Scrivens now leads from the front to get rid of a dangerous batter in Shweta Sehrawat. India Women Under-19 might feel a bit uncomfortable at the moment. It is flatter and on off, turning in a touch. Shweta Sehrawat is caught inside her crease. She tries to flick it away but it comes off the top-edge. Hannah L Baker takes an easy catch at short fine leg.
Commentary.Howout: c Hannah L Baker b Grace Scrivens

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Glorious shot. It is a low full toss, on off. Shweta Sehrawat leans in and creams it through the cover region for a boundary.
Floats it up, outside off. The ball holds in the surface a touch. Shweta Sehrawat defends it to cover on her front foot.
Loopy ball, on off, helped back to the bowler.
Grace Scrivens brings herself into the attack.
Around off, tapped out to point. A wicket-maiden for Hannah L Baker. Just what the doctor ordered for England Women Under-19. Will they be able to put a lid over the run rate here?
Soumya Tiwari presses forward and drives this full ball to covers.
Swing and a miss! This is tossed up, in the channel. Tiwari looks to chase it but gets beaten in the process.
Floats it up, full and on off. It grips and turns away. Tiwari leaves it alone.
On off, defended out watchfully.
Soumya Tiwari walks in at number 3 for India Women Under-19.

OUT! CAUGHT! Hannah L Baker draws first blood here. A glimmer of hope for England Women Under-19. They are delighted to see the back of Shafali Verma here. It is tossed up, on middle and leg. Shafali Verma shuffles but ends up chipping it to the left of mid on, as her bat turned in her hand. Alexa Stonehouse there gets low to her right and takes a sharp catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Alexa Stonehouse b Hannah L Baker

Commentary.Commentary: A low full toss, on middle. Verma works it down to long on and crosses. She retains the strike here.
SIX! BANG! Shafali Verma gets this first maximum off the chase. It is pitched up, full and on off. Verma launches it past over long off fence for a biggie.
On off, pushed back to the right of the bowler.
Floated and full, on middle and leg. Verma whips it to deep mid-wicket. The fielder in the deep fumbles and they collect a brace.
Around off, this is pushed down to mid off for one.
Fuller, on middle and leg. Verma clips it to the leg side for a single now.
Sophia Smale will operate from the other end.
This is tossed up, outside off. Shweta Sehrawat tries to drive it through the line but misses.
It is looped up, around off. Verma smacks it down to long on for a single.
Shafali Verma taps this full ball to covers.
Incredible turn! It drifts in, lands on middle and turns away. Varma tries to clip it away but misses. She gets pinged high on her pads.
Pushed through quicker and full, outside off. Verma tries to have a poke at it but misses.
FOUR! Easy pickings! Shafali Verma and India Women Under-19 get off the mark instantly. It is spilled down leg, on a length. Shafali Verma tickles it down to fine leg for four runs.
